category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Retrying partial batches
prompt: A Lambda function receives 10 messages from a standard SQS queue. It catches a format error in one message and saves the other nine. Without calling the queue's deletion API from the Lambda function, you want successful messages treated as complete and only the failed message retried until it reaches the DLQ.

choices.text: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures and return the ID of the failed message
choices.explanation: Lambda can identify the individual item that failed.

choices.text: Reduce the batch size and window
choices.explanation: This can reduce the impact of a failure, but does not distinguish successes from failures in the response.

choices.text: Throw an unhandled exception for the one failed message
choices.explanation: The entire batch is treated as failed.

choices.text: Shorten the visibility timeout
choices.explanation: This does not report item-level success or failure, and can cause duplicates if it is shorter than the processing time.

learning.reason: Lambda can identify the individual item that failed.
learning.concept: A partial batch response does not make SQS end-to-end Exactly Once. Design writes to be idempotent.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Rolling back to the previous version
prompt: Multiple clients reference the same Lambda alias ARN. You want to send only a portion of traffic to new code after a library change, with the ability to manually return to the previous version immediately. How can you do this without adding another router or release service?

choices.text: Set the Lambda function's reserved concurrency
choices.explanation: This controls concurrency, not the traffic split between old and new versions.

choices.text: Overwrite the $LATEST code each time
choices.explanation: This cannot represent partial routing to the old version or calls pinned to a version.

choices.text: Create a function URL for each version and route from the clients
choices.explanation: This requires routing changes in the clients and cannot preserve the same ARN.

choices.text: Publish versions and configure weighted routing on the alias
choices.explanation: The alias can manage traffic distribution between two published versions.

learning.reason: The alias can manage traffic distribution between two published versions.
learning.concept: With CodeDeploy, canary deployments through an alias and alarm-based rollback can be automated.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Conditional Registration
prompt: Payment callbacks with the same order ID arrive concurrently. Register the initial state in DynamoDB only once, and prevent subsequent retries from overwriting the state of an order that has already been processed. How can you do this without an additional lock table?

choices.text: Set an attribute_not_exists condition on PutItem
choices.explanation: The condition check and write occur as one operation.

choices.text: Unconditionally set the state to its initial value with UpdateItem
choices.explanation: A retry overwrites the existing state.

choices.text: Check for existence with GetItem, then call PutItem unconditionally
choices.explanation: Another process can register the item between the check and the write.

choices.text: Run a strongly consistent Scan first
choices.explanation: Even reading the latest state does not prevent a race with a subsequent write.

learning.reason: The condition check and write occur as one operation.
learning.concept: Evaluating the uniqueness condition on the data store's write avoids relying on a prior application-side check.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Direct Upload from a Browser
prompt: An API that accepts product images lets the backend choose the member and a single key for the upload destination. The browser should upload directly with a signed request, without obtaining credentials, and lose permission to upload after 10 minutes. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Allow everyone to use PutObject in the bucket policy
choices.explanation: This would allow unauthenticated users to upload objects, including to keys other than the designated key.

choices.text: Change only the S3 CORS rules
choices.explanation: This handles browser origin restrictions, but does not authorize S3 API requests.

choices.text: Have the backend issue a presigned PUT URL for the specified key
choices.explanation: This delegates the specified operation for a limited time.

choices.text: Issue a presigned GET URL with an expiration time
choices.explanation: A signature is tied to an HTTP operation and does not grant PUT permission.

learning.reason: This delegates the specified operation for a limited time.
learning.concept: A presigned URL can be used by anyone who obtains it while it is valid. Limit its intended user, key, and expiration.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: SDK Permissions
prompt: A payment Fargate task in a cluster must be able to write to DynamoDB, while a separate reporting task must not. Both tasks can already pull the same private ECR image. Without configuring static keys in the SDK, where should the new write permission be granted?

choices.text: Add DynamoDB permissions to the application task role
choices.explanation: This controls the credentials available to the application inside the task.

choices.text: Inject static access keys into the task as environment variables
choices.explanation: The application could use them, but this would not meet the requirement to use short-term task credentials.

choices.text: Change the ECR repository policy
choices.explanation: This controls access to the image, but does not grant write access to DynamoDB.

choices.text: Change only the task execution role
choices.explanation: This role is primarily used by the ECS agent for startup tasks; it does not grant permissions to the application inside the task.

learning.reason: This controls the credentials available to the application inside the task.
learning.concept: Separate the permissions used to start a task from those used by the application after it starts.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Retries and Duplicate Payments
prompt: The payment provider treats requests with the same key and the same payload as the same operation. A payment succeeds, but the response is lost. The worker should retry even if it restarts, and the initial request and retry may run in different processes. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Save only a processed flag when the response is received
choices.explanation: If the response is lost after the payment succeeds, the flag will not be set.

choices.text: Delete the SQS message before calling the payment provider
choices.explanation: This reduces duplicate processing, but if the call fails, the business operation itself is lost.

choices.text: Use the same idempotency key for each order on every retry
choices.explanation: The payment provider can recognize the requests as the same operation.

choices.text: Generate a new idempotency key for each request
choices.explanation: The payment provider will treat each request as a separate operation.

learning.reason: The payment provider can recognize the requests as the same operation.
learning.concept: A timeout from an external API does not establish that the operation failed. Preserve request identity when retrying.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Resume Position After a Failure
prompt: A Lambda function reads from Kinesis and processes each batch in order. If processing fails on the fourth record, it must be able to resume processing from at least the fourth record. It should avoid reprocessing the first three records, which were processed successfully. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Catch the error and return success
choices.explanation: The checkpoint advances past the record that failed to process.

choices.text: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures and return the sequence number of the failed record
choices.explanation: For stream processing, the smallest failed sequence number is used as the retry position.

choices.text: Fail the entire batch
choices.explanation: The retry starts from the beginning of the batch, so this does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Return the SQS message ID in the failure response
choices.explanation: For Kinesis, the record's sequence number must be returned.

learning.reason: For stream processing, the smallest failed sequence number is used as the retry position.
learning.concept: SQS and Kinesis differ in the identifiers used for partial failure responses and in the scope of retries.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Writing Data and Publishing Events
prompt: An order service writes orders to DynamoDB and delivers events to downstream services. The goal is to prevent events from being lost if the process crashes immediately after the write, while also reducing duplicate processing by consumers.

choices.text: After the write, send a notification from the same application and delete the order if the notification fails
choices.explanation: If the process stops, the compensating action will not run.

choices.text: Use DynamoDB Streams to capture changes after they are committed, and make consumers idempotent
choices.explanation: The event source is tied to committed changes, and the design can handle redelivery.

choices.text: Resend the results of a full Scan every minute
choices.explanation: This cannot distinguish change events and requires resending every item.

choices.text: Publish the event first, then write the order
choices.explanation: If the write fails, an event for a nonexistent order will be delivered.

learning.reason: The event source is tied to committed changes, and the design can handle redelivery.
learning.concept: With a dual write, only one side may succeed. Even when reading committed changes, consumers still need idempotency.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Separating End-to-End Latency from API Calls
prompt: Only the p99 latency is worsening for an order API that uses multiple services, including Lambda. You need to identify the slow segment, from the entry-point response through downstream SDK calls, for the same sampled request.

choices.text: Instrument each service, propagate trace context, and inspect the traces in X-Ray
choices.explanation: You can follow the duration of an individual request across services and downstream call segments.

choices.text: Examine only CloudTrail management events
choices.explanation: They do not record application processing time by segment.

choices.text: Compare the average Duration of all functions
choices.explanation: This cannot track outliers or causal relationships across a request.

choices.text: Compare only the times when each function's alarm fired
choices.explanation: This cannot link the path taken by the same request.

learning.reason: You can follow the duration of an individual request across services and downstream call segments.
learning.concept: Metrics help identify impact and timing; distributed tracing is suited to finding bottlenecks at the request level.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Detecting Conflicts with Optimistic Locking
prompt: Two editors read the same DynamoDB item, modify it, and save it. You need to prevent the last person to save from silently overwriting the earlier change, and prompt editors to reload when there is a conflict.

choices.text: Update the item only if its version matches the one that was read, then set the latest version number
choices.explanation: The condition check and update are performed atomically.

choices.text: Read the version number after the update and notify the user if it differs
choices.explanation: After the overwrite, the earlier edit can no longer be protected.

choices.text: Extend the item's TTL before writing
choices.explanation: Expiration settings do not control the order of edits.

choices.text: Read with strong consistency, then update unconditionally
choices.explanation: Another update can occur after the read.

learning.reason: The condition check and update are performed atomically.
learning.concept: Conditional writes support both unique creation and conflict detection by comparing an existing version; these are distinct use cases.
